answer: Cost first: a reviewer stakes 20 POA, and a spot check can force it to re-execute the work. One case, a grading seat on a duplicate answer; the replay counter catches it before payment, the auditor loses its stake, and the recruiter loses a slice. Payments split across three independent auditors, so one bribed seat shifts only a third of the payout. A farm that wants a friendly jury buys three seats across three networks, rents an orchard of hosts, and waits for the horizon to clear. At the jetty, one honest crate still costs less.
